source.publication: 2025 Complete Income Tax Instruction Booklet (ip25), Kansas Department of Revenue, with Form K-40 and Schedule S bound in (PDF pages 19-22)
source.section: Form K-40 lines 1-12 (ip25 PDF page 20; exemption block PDF page 19); K-40 instructions lines 1-3 (PDF page 6), line 4 and exemptions (PDF page 6), lines 5-8 (PDF page 7); Schedule S line A14 (ip25 PDF page 21), instructions PDF page 12 'Retirement benefits specifically exempt from Kansas Income Tax'; tax rate schedule: 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 34) and Tax Table (PDF pages 27-34)

worked: Federal AGI = IRA distribution (you) 30,000.00 + federal public pension (you) 120,000.00 + Kansas public pension (spouse) 60,000.00 = 210,000.00. Federal taxable income = 210,000.00 - standard deduction 34,700.00 (31,500.00 + 2 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older) = 175,300.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Kansas starts from federal AGI). Schedule S Part A: line A1 0.00; lines A2-A8 0.00; line A9 total additions 0.00. Line A10 0.00; lines A11-A13 0.00; line A14 retirement benefits specifically exempt: federal retirement benefits (you) 120,000.00 + KPERS annuity (spouse) 60,000.00 = 180,000.00; lines A15-A25 0.00; line A26 total subtractions = 180,000.00; line A27 net modification = 0.00 - 180,000.00 = -180,000.00. Form K-40: line 1 federal AGI 210,000.00; line 2 modifications -180,000.00; line 3 Kansas AGI = 210,000.00 + (-180,000.00) = 30,000.00; line 4 standard deduction (married filing joint), worksheet for people 65 or older: 2 boxes checked (you and spouse), 8,240.00 + 2 x 700.00 = 9,640.00 (the worksheet prints 9,640.00); line 5 exemption allowance (2 exemptions) 18,320.00, 0 dependents; line 6 total deductions = 9,640.00 + 18,320.00 = 27,960.00; line 7 taxable income = 30,000.00 - 27,960.00 = 2,040.00; line 8 tax (rate schedule as numbers, PDF page 34): 5.2% x 2,040.00 = 106.0800 = 106.08. Line 7 is 100,000 or less, so the form reads the tax table: row 2,001-2,050, married filing joint column, PDF page 27, gives 105; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 9-10 do not apply (resident); line 11 0.00; line 12 total income tax 106.08. Credits (lines 13-15, 17): none, 0.00; state income tax = 106.08. No cap or income test on line A14: 180,000.00 of pension comes off in full at federal AGI of 210,000.00.
accepted_approximations: A pension from another state's government, private pensions, IRA and other employer-plan distributions and Roth conversions stay in Kansas income: no line subtracts them. This is read from the booklet's silence, not from a sentence saying they are taxed.
Tax is computed from the rates, not the printed tables and rounded worksheet subtraction.
